statement_analysis.reason: दोनों साम्राज्य बार-बार तुंगभद्रा को पार करते रहे, भले ही यह सीमा के रूप में संधियों में उल्लेखित था, जो दर्शाता है कि यह एक प्रतीकात्मक संदर्भ बिंदु था न कि लागू क्षेत्रीय सीमा।

hi.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प d (1, 2 और 3) एक मजबूत भ्रम है क्योंकि जो छात्र कथन 1 और 3 को सही मानते हैं, वे कथन 2 के 'स्थायी क्षेत्रीय समझौता' के गलत दावे का सावधानीपूर्वक मूल्यांकन नहीं कर सकते।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 सत्यापित करें — कृषि अधिशेष, कर राजस्व, और बफर की भूमिका दोआब की रणनीतिक अस्वीकार्यता के स्थापित कारण हैं। कथन 1 सही है।
कथन 2 की जांच करें — 'हमेशा स्थायी क्षेत्रीय समझौता' वाक्यांश दोआब के बार-बार बदलने के पैटर्न के विपरीत है। कथन 2 गलत है।
कथन 3 सत्यापित करें — दोनों साम्राज्यों द्वारा तुंगभद्रा को स्थायी सीमा के रूप में स्वीकार न करना एक मुख्य ऐतिहासिक तथ्य है। कथन 3 सही है।
कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं — विकल्प (a) चुनें।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 में 'हमेशा' और 'स्थायी' शब्दों का दायरा बढ़ाने वाला जाल है, जो सैन्य विजय के होने को स्थायी परिणामों के रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है। वास्तव में, दोआब संघर्ष की विशेषता हर सैन्य समझौते की अस्थिरता है — 'हमेशा स्थायी' ऐतिहासिक रूप से इसके विपरीत है।
hi.final_explanation:
रायचूर दोआब का महत्व और तुंगभद्रा सीमा उल्लंघनों का पैटर्न विजयनगर–बहमनी क्षेत्रीय संघर्ष के दो सबसे परीक्षणीय पहलू हैं।

• कथन 1 — सही: दोआब एक साथ कृषि-राजस्व संपत्ति और सैन्य बफर क्षेत्र था, जो दोनों साम्राज्यों के लिए इसे अस्वीकार्य बनाता था — यह संयोजन कूटनीतिक समाधान को संरचनात्मक रूप से असंभव बनाता है।
• कथन 2 — गलत: दोआब में सैन्य विजय स्थायी समझौते उत्पन्न करने में विफल रही — यह पैटर्न है, अपवाद नहीं। दोआब कई बार बदलता रहा, प्रत्येक विजेता अंततः नियंत्रण खोता रहा।
• कथन 3 — सही: तुंगभद्रा को शांति संधियों में स्थायी सीमा के रूप में बार-बार उल्लेखित किया गया, फिर भी दोनों साम्राज्य इसे पार करते रहे, जिससे यह एक प्रतीकात्मक सीमा बनी न कि लागू क्षेत्रीय सीमा।

Value Addition:
• दोआब का बार-बार बदलना कभी-कभी दोनों साम्राज्यों के बीच रणनीतिक संतुलन के प्रमाण के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया जाता है — कोई भी स्थायी प्रभुत्व स्थापित नहीं कर पाया।
• तुंगभद्रा को सीमा के रूप में बार-बार संधि में उल्लेख करना दर्शाता है कि दोनों पक्ष इसे प्राकृतिक सीमा के रूप में मानते थे, लेकिन लागू सीमा के रूप में स्वीकार नहीं कर पाए।
• कृष्णदेवराय का 1520 में रायचूर पर कब्जा दोआब नियंत्रण का सबसे प्रसिद्ध उदाहरण है — और यह भी कुछ वर्षों में उलट गया।

shared.concept_anchor: Fernao Nuniz visited Achyuta Raya — not Krishnadevaraya

en.display_text:
Consider the following two statements about Portuguese sources for Vijayanagara history:

Statement 1: Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa are Portuguese sources who documented Vijayanagara's military strength and court during Krishnadevaraya's reign, providing contemporaneous eyewitness accounts of the early 16th century empire.

Statement 2: Fernão Nunes (Nuniz), another Portuguese chronicler, visited Vijayanagara during Krishnadevaraya's reign and his account specifically covers the Raichur campaign of 1520.

Which of the following is correct?

(a) Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
(b) Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are incorrect
(c) Statement 1 is incorrect but Statement 2 is correct
(d) Statement 1 is correct but Statement 2 is incorrect

statement_analysis.statement: Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa are Portuguese sources who documented Vijayanagara's military strength and court during Krishnadevaraya's reign, providing contemporaneous eyewitness accounts of the early 16th century empire.
statement_analysis.reason: Both Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa visited Vijayanagara during or around Krishnadevaraya's reign and left accounts of the empire's military capacity and royal court, making them reliable contemporaneous sources for that period.

statement_analysis.statement: Fernão Nunes (Nuniz), another Portuguese chronicler, visited Vijayanagara during Krishnadevaraya's reign and his account specifically covers the Raichur campaign of 1520.
statement_analysis.reason: Fernão Nunes visited Vijayanagara during Achyuta Raya's reign, not Krishnadevaraya's; his account therefore does not cover the 1520 Raichur campaign, which predates his visit.

en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (both correct) is a strong distractor because all three Portuguese travelers are frequently grouped together in UPSC preparation materials as 'eyewitnesses to Vijayanagara,' leading students to assume they all visited during the same reign.
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 1 — Paes and Barbosa as contemporaneous sources for Krishnadevaraya's reign is historically established. Statement 1 is correct.

Examine Statement 2 — Fernão Nunes visited during Achyuta Raya's reign, not Krishnadevaraya's; his account is for a different period and cannot cover the 1520 Raichur campaign. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Statement 1 correct, Statement 2 incorrect — select option (d).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The entity-swap trap substitutes Krishnadevaraya for Achyuta Raya as the ruler during whose reign Fernão Nunes visited. Students who group all three Portuguese travelers (Paes, Barbosa, Nuniz) as 'Krishnadevaraya-era sources' will accept Statement 2 without noticing the critical distinction between their respective visit periods.
en.final_explanation:
The three principal Portuguese sources for Vijayanagara history — Domingo Paes, Duarte Barbosa, and Fernão Nunes — are frequently conflated in UPSC preparation, but they visited during different reigns and cover different periods.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Paes and Barbosa both visited during or around Krishnadevaraya's reign (early 16th century) and are the primary Portuguese eyewitness sources for his military capacity and the Raichur campaign.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Fernão Nunes visited Vijayanagara during Achyuta Raya's reign (Krishnadevaraya's successor). His account covers a later period and cannot describe the 1520 Raichur campaign.

Value Addition:
• A memory device: Paes + Barbosa = Krishnadevaraya; Nuniz = Achyuta Raya.
• Achyuta Raya succeeded Krishnadevaraya around 1529; Nuniz visited in the early 1530s.
• Fernão Nunes provided valuable administrative and dynastic history of Vijayanagara but is not an eyewitness to the Raichur campaign — this distinction is a classic UPSC trap.

en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the impact of the Bahmani Sultanate's fragmentation on the Vijayanagara Empire:

1. The fragmentation of the Bahmani Sultanate into five successor states from the 1490s onward gave Vijayanagara a strategic advantage in the short term, as it now faced divided rivals rather than a unified adversary.
2. The eventual military confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates that defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota in 1565 was a resurgence of the Bahmani Sultanate under a new name, not a coalition of independent successor states.
3. Krishnadevaraya's capture of Raichur in 1520 was fought against Bijapur, a successor state of the Bahmani Sultanate, rather than against the Bahmani Sultanate directly.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: The fragmentation of the Bahmani Sultanate into five successor states from the 1490s onward gave Vijayanagara a strategic advantage in the short term, as it now faced divided rivals rather than a unified adversary.
statement_analysis.reason: Dealing with fragmented successor states individually was strategically easier for Vijayanagara than confronting a unified Bahmani Sultanate; this advantage is evidenced by Krishnadevaraya's successful Raichur campaign of 1520 against the weakened Bijapur Sultanate.

statement_analysis.statement: The eventual military confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates that defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota in 1565 was a resurgence of the Bahmani Sultanate under a new name, not a coalition of independent successor states.
statement_analysis.reason: The Talikota confederacy comprised independent successor states (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, and Bidar) acting in temporary alliance — it was not a resurgence of the Bahmani Sultanate as a unified political entity, which had permanently dissolved.

statement_analysis.statement: Krishnadevaraya's capture of Raichur in 1520 was fought against Bijapur, a successor state of the Bahmani Sultanate, rather than against the Bahmani Sultanate directly.
statement_analysis.reason: By 1520 the Bahmani Sultanate had fragmented; the Raichur region was controlled by Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur, making the 1520 campaign a Vijayanagara–Bijapur conflict, not a direct Vijayanagara–Bahmani confrontation.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d (1, 2 and 3) is the strongest distractor because Statement 2 sounds plausible — 'resurgence under a new name' is a familiar historical pattern students may have encountered in other contexts and may apply here without scrutiny.
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 1 — Vijayanagara's strategic advantage from Bahmani fragmentation is historically evident from the successful 1520 Raichur campaign. Statement 1 is correct.

Examine Statement 2 — the Talikota confederacy was a coalition of independent successor states, not a reconstituted Bahmani Sultanate; the Bahmani Sultanate permanently ceased to exist as a unified entity. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Verify Statement 3 — the 1520 Raichur campaign was against Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur, a Bahmani successor state, not the Bahmani Sultanate directly. Statement 3 is correct.
Statements 1 and 3 are correct — select option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The temporal-swap trap in Statement 2 implies a historical continuity (Bahmani → reconstituted under new name) that did not occur. The Bahmani Sultanate's fragmentation was permanent. Students who are accustomed to dynasties reconsolidating after fragmentation (e.g., Mughal revival attempts) may apply this pattern to the Bahmani case, accepting the false 'resurgence' framing.
en.final_explanation:
The Bahmani Sultanate's fragmentation changed the strategic landscape of the Deccan permanently, creating both opportunities and eventual threats for Vijayanagara.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Fragmentation into five successor states gave Vijayanagara a short-term strategic advantage — evidenced by the successful 1520 Raichur campaign against the weakened Bijapur Sultanate.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: The Talikota confederacy was a temporary military alliance of independent states (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar) — not a reconstituted Bahmani Sultanate. The Bahmani Sultanate as a political entity had permanently dissolved.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The 1520 Raichur campaign was specifically against Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur — a critical distinction because it means the famous campaign was fought against a Bahmani successor state, not the Bahmani Sultanate itself.

Value Addition:
• The five Deccan Sultanates: Ahmadnagar, Bidar, Bijapur, Berar, Golconda — emerged between the 1490s and 1510s.
• The temporary Deccan Sultanate confederacy at Talikota dissolved immediately after their victory — the five states resumed mutual rivalries.
• Vijayanagara's strategic advantage from Bahmani fragmentation was ultimately reversed by the confederacy formation — a classic example of the balance-of-power dynamic.

Assertion (a): Early Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflicts are frequently confused in historical accounts with Delhi Sultanate–Deccan conflicts of the same period, due to chronological and territorial overlap.

Reason (R): Both the Vijayanagara Empire and the Bahmani Sultanate emerged from the power vacuum created by the Delhi Sultanate's weakening control over the Deccan in the 1330s–1340s.

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A

(d) A is incorrect but R is correct

A is correct.

Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? — Both the Vijayanagara Empire and the Bahmani Sultanate did emerge from the power vacuum left by the Delhi Sultanate's weakening Deccan control; this is historically accurate. R is correct.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? — R explains the structural context of both empires' emergence but does not explain WHY the early conflicts are confused with Delhi Sultanate conflicts in historical accounts. en.display_text:
Consider the following statements about the historiographical debate over the nature of the Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflict:

1. The presence of Muslim commanders in Vijayanagara's armies and Hindu vassals in Bahmani service is cited by modern historians as evidence contradicting the interpretation of Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflicts as a purely religious civilizational war.
2. Colonial and some medieval historians who framed Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflicts as a Hindu–Muslim civilizational war were fully supported by modern archaeology and epigraphy, which have confirmed this interpretation.
3. The opportunistic timing of military campaigns to coincide with succession crises in the rival polity is considered evidence supporting the territorial-realist interpretation rather than the religious-war thesis of the Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflict.

Which of the above statements is/are NOT correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 2 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 2 and 3 only

statement_analysis.statement: The presence of Muslim commanders in Vijayanagara's armies and Hindu vassals in Bahmani service is cited by modern historians as evidence contradicting the interpretation of Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflicts as a purely religious civilizational war.
statement_analysis.reason: Cross-religious military service on both sides is a standard empirical argument used by historians including Romila Thapar and Burton Stein to refute the civilizational conflict thesis.

statement_analysis.statement: Colonial and some medieval historians who framed Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflicts as a Hindu–Muslim civilizational war were fully supported by modern archaeology and epigraphy, which have confirmed this interpretation.
statement_analysis.reason: Modern archaeology and epigraphy have not confirmed the religious-war framing; on the contrary, inscriptional and material evidence of composite culture, cross-religious service, and pragmatic statecraft have generally undermined the civilizational conflict thesis.

statement_analysis.statement: The opportunistic timing of military campaigns to coincide with succession crises in the rival polity is considered evidence supporting the territorial-realist interpretation rather than the religious-war thesis of the Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflict.
statement_analysis.reason: Exploiting succession crises is quintessentially pragmatic and power-political behavior that is inconsistent with ideologically driven religious war, making it a key argument for the realist interpretation.

en.strong_distractor: a — Option a (1 only) is a strong distractor because students who quickly read Statement 1 as the obviously correct one and the question asking for the NOT-correct answer may select it without fully evaluating Statement 2.
elimination_logic: The question asks which is NOT correct.
Evaluate Statement 1 — cross-religious military service as evidence against the civilizational war thesis is established historiography. Statement 1 IS correct, so it is not the NOT-correct answer.

Evaluate Statement 2 — claiming modern archaeology and epigraphy 'fully supported' and 'confirmed' the religious-war interpretation inverts the historical record; the evidence has broadly undermined it. Statement 2 is NOT correct.
Evaluate Statement 3 — succession-crisis timing as evidence for the realist interpretation is established. Statement 3 IS correct. The NOT-correct statement is 2 only — select option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The scope-extension trap in Statement 2 uses 'fully supported' and 'confirmed' to transform a false claim into one that sounds definitive and authoritative. Students who know that archaeology and epigraphy are used in medieval historical analysis may not immediately register that their evidence actually undermines, rather than confirms, the religious-war thesis.
en.final_explanation:
Modern historiography has progressively dismantled the purely religious-war interpretation of the Vijayanagara–Bahmani conflicts using multiple categories of evidence.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Cross-religious military service (Muslim commanders in Vijayanagara, Hindu vassals under Bahmani rulers) is one of the strongest empirical arguments against the civilizational conflict thesis.
• Statement 2 — NOT Correct: Modern archaeology and epigraphy have not confirmed the religious-war interpretation — the evidence of composite culture, shared administrative practices, and cross-religious military service has broadly undermined it. 'Fully supported and confirmed' is the false element.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Opportunistic succession-crisis timing of military campaigns is the strongest behavioral evidence for territorial-realist rather than ideological-religious motivations in the conflict.

Value Addition:
• The religious-war framing was particularly prominent in colonial-era histories (James Grant Duff's Marathas, Firishta's readings) and was used for political purposes.
• Post-independence Indian historiography, led by Romila Thapar, Irfan Habib, and Burton Stein, systematically challenged this framing.
• Composite culture (architectural, administrative, military borrowing) is the positive evidence; succession-exploitation is the behavioral evidence — together they constitute a comprehensive refutation.

कथन 3 का मूल्यांकन करें — उत्तराधिकार संकट के समय का यथार्थवादी व्याख्या के लिए साक्ष्य के रूप में होना स्थापित है। कथन 3 सही है। गलत कथन केवल 2 है — विकल्प (b) चुनें।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 में स्कोप-एक्सटेंशन ट्रैप 'पूर्ण समर्थन' और 'पुष्टि' शब्दों का उपयोग करके एक गलत दावे को निर्णायक और अधिकारिक लगने वाला बना देता है। जो छात्र जानते हैं कि मध्यकालीन ऐतिहासिक विश्लेषण में पुरातत्व और शिलालेखों का उपयोग होता है, वे तुरंत यह नहीं समझ पाते कि उनका साक्ष्य वास्तव में धार्मिक-युद्ध सिद्धांत को कमजोर करता है, न कि पुष्टि।

• कथन 1 — सही: धर्म-परस्पर सैन्य सेवा (विजयनगर में मुस्लिम कमांडर, बहमनी शासकों के अधीन हिंदू अधीनस्थ) सभ्यतागत संघर्ष सिद्धांत के विरुद्ध सबसे मजबूत अनुभवजन्य तर्कों में से एक है।
• कथन 2 — सही नहीं: आधुनिक पुरातत्व और शिलालेखों ने धार्मिक-युद्ध व्याख्या की पुष्टि नहीं की है — मिश्रित संस्कृति, साझा प्रशासनिक प्रथाओं, और धर्म-परस्पर सैन्य सेवा के साक्ष्यों ने इसे व्यापक रूप से कमजोर किया है। 'पूर्ण समर्थन और पुष्टि' गलत तत्व है।
• कथन 3 — सही: उत्तराधिकार संकट के अवसरवादी समय का सैन्य अभियानों के लिए होना संघर्ष में वैचारिक-धार्मिक प्रेरणाओं के बजाय क्षेत्रीय-यथार्थवादी कारणों के लिए सबसे मजबूत व्यवहारिक साक्ष्य है।

Value Addition:
